extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, prospective Oberwolfach participants, graduate students and postdocs
extracted.subtask_description: Annual program and informational report for the Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach (MFO) describing workshop schedules, student support, publication formats (Oberwolfach Reports), prizes, and related program policies for 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Leibniz Graduate Students eligibility and reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the beginning of 2009, the MFO has been supporting the participation of an average of five doctoral students per Oberwolfach Workshop. This program fosters excellent graduate students and recent post docs (the Ph.D./Dr. degree must be received not more than two years ago). For this program, each Oberwolfach Workshop is given an extra capacity of five places which may not be taken by senior researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target: excellent doctoral students or recent Ph.D.s (no more than two years after the degree). Each workshop has five additional reserved places for Oberwolfach Leibniz Graduate Students; these reserved places are explicitly not to be occupied by established/senior researchers. The program in particular provides reimbursement of travel costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost support for graduate participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The program fosters excellent graduate students and recent post docs ... in particular by the reimbursement of travel costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel cost reimbursement is part of the support offered to eligible Leibniz Graduate Students; used as an explicit eligibility/benefit criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Reports (OWR) content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Oberwolfach Reports (OWR) ... are comprised of official reports of every workshop, containing extended abstracts of the given talks, of one up to three pages per talk, including references. They appear quarterly in an edition of 300 copies. The 4 issues comprise more than 3,000 pages per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission/coverage expectation: each talk is documented by an extended abstract (1–3 pages) and must include literature references. OWRs serve to document the scientific level of events and to disseminate results presented at the institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Prize and John Todd Award eligibility and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Oberwolfach Prize is awarded by the Gesellschaft für Mathematische Forschung e.V. and by the Oberwolfach Foundation to European junior researchers. The prize is awarded for excellent achievements in changing fields of mathematics. The Oberwolfach Foundation awards in cooperation with the MFO approximately every three years the John Todd Award to junior scientists in numerical analysis. The Oberwolfach Prize amounts to 10,000 Euro and the John Todd Award to 1,000 Euro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility: European junior researchers (prize) and junior researchers in numerical analysis (John Todd Award). Frequency: roughly every three years. Purpose: recognize 'excellent achievements' in rotating/changing mathematical fields; monetary endowments specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program representation policy (coverage of mathematical fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute emphasizes that all fields of mathematics and related areas are represented, including applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and program planning are guided by a policy to include the full breadth of mathematical disciplines and their applications; the annual program is presented to evidence this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and durations of events in the annual program
rubrics_metrics.description: In the year 2015 43 workshops have taken place during 41 weeks, as well as 12 Mini-Workshops during four weeks, 6 Oberwolfach Seminars during three weeks and 2 Arbeitsgemeinschaften during 2 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program structure: distinguishes Workshops, Miniworkshops, Oberwolfach Seminars, and Arbeitsgemeinschaften with typical durations (workshops ~1 week, miniworkshops grouped into specified weeks, seminars typically three weeks, Arbeitsgemeinschaften two weeks). Useful for planning submissions/participation and for authors preparing OWR entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop objectives and expected scope (abstract guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop abstracts describe aims such as focusing on interplay between subfields, discussing and comparing novel approaches, studying potential and applicability, formulating strategic goals and directions of research for the next five years, presenting latest results, and emphasizing connections to applications or other branches of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From multiple workshop abstracts: expected aims include (depending on the workshop) presenting recent advances, exchanging methods, highlighting interplay between areas (e.g., geometry and group theory), discussing open problems, and setting short- to mid-term research directions. Abstracts should state focus, scope, and intended outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop reporting contents (what each workshop entry includes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each workshop entry in the report includes an Abstract (describing focus and aims) and a Participants list (names and affiliations), as well as Organizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For documentation purposes (OWR and annual report) each workshop record should supply an abstract of the workshop topics and a full participants list plus organizers; abstracts vary in length and should summarize goals, highlights, and key topics.
